annotation.authors_or_issuer: International Working Group on Data Protection in Technology (Berlin Group), secretariat at the Federal Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information (BfDI), Germany
key_provisions_or_claims: Cities should conduct data protection impact assessments before processing and review them when new technology is introduced.
Data minimisation: aggregate and strip identifiers early, with embedded technical measures and automated deletion.
Purpose limitation: compatibility assessments are needed before reusing data, and consent or a legal basis is needed for new purposes.
Procurement should require security standards, audits, patchability and no default passwords for IoT devices.
Cities should give transparency at the point of collection and respect individual rights, and regulators should issue guidance.
annotation.summary_en: Working paper of the International Working Group on Data Protection in Technology (Berlin Group) on smart cities. It sets out data protection principles across data collection, analysis and decision. It gives case studies (Enschede, TfL, Toronto, Helsinki) and recommendations for cities, industry and regulators on accountability, minimisation, purpose limitation, security, transparency and individual rights.
